verdict_note: From reading only: no build and no tests were run. Line anchors are crates/hsk-studio-layout/src/threaded_reflow.rs at a7de5fcd. The core fix holds. In compose, every baseline comes from next_slot, which floors extra at -(line * height) (:458) before baseline_of (:394), and baseline_of clamps to the column's first baseline. Balancing floors per row (:900-911) and uses the same baseline_of. All four composers only break lines into those slots, so no composer can put a baseline above the column's first baseline. Overset stays the next_slot outcome: a lifted paragraph steps down from the column top, and what does not fit moves to the next column or frame and finally to overset. The probe reading holds: 10 lines placed, overset 30..119. The floor only bites when the line's computed baseline would lie above base, so a legitimate negative gap that keeps lines inside the column is unchanged. NaN and infinity are refused before the floor (length_pt, styles.rs:67-79; sum; balance_band's is_finite). Removing Cursor.gaps reopens no non-finite path, because the floor bounds extra from below. One medium defect, F1, belongs to the same R60 class: lines outside the frame while overset is None. vertical_justify (:933-985) sizes a column's block from its first and last lines in index order. A negative gap, legitimate or clamped by this fix, can leave the last line above an earlier one, and then Bottom, Center or Justify move earlier lines below the frame bottom. The bug is present at the base, but the lane's V4-06 list marks the site not applicable for a reason that does not hold. F2 and F3 are low: F2 is a reading gap (the floor bounds the baseline, not the line box) and F3 is a test gap.

findings.what: vertical_justify assumes that a column's lines descend in index order: the first line is the top of the block and the last line is its bottom. A negative paragraph gap breaks that assumption, and this lane's floor does too, because it stacks a lifted paragraph on the column's first baseline over earlier lines. The block bottom is then underestimated, the slack is overestimated, and the shift moves the real deepest lines past the inset bottom. overset is decided before this point, so it stays None. By reading, the existing mixed-leading reading of baseline_of can also produce such a column with no negative space: P0 at line height 12 gives 10, 22, 34, and a following line-height-4 line at line 3 gives 10 + 12 = 22. That route is noted only; it is outside this lane.
findings.scenario:
A one-column 120 x 100 pt frame with fixed first baseline 10 (the test font: line height 12, ascent 10) and vertical_justification Bottom. The story is 'aa
', 'bb
', 'cc
' (style 1) and 'dd' (space_before -1000). Compose gives baselines 10, 22, 34, 10 and overset None. The block is measured as [0, 12], so slack is 88 and dy is 88, giving baselines 98, 110, 122, 98. Lines 2 and 3 have boxes ending at 112 and 124 in a 100 pt frame, and overset is None. Center is shown with 8 lines (10..94) plus a lifted ninth line at 10: dy is 44, so the line at 94 moves to 138. With a legitimate in-column gap of -30 on 'dd' at the base, the baselines are 10, 22, 34, 16, Bottom gives dy 82, and 'cc' lands at 116.
findings.fix: In vertical_justify, measure the block as the minimum (baseline - ascent) and maximum (baseline + descent) over the column's lines, as the span band (:1242) and autosize already do. With that block, Center and Bottom keep every box inside the inset. Justify then gives the line with the last index the full slack, and every earlier line a smaller shift, which keeps it at or above the true bottom. The alternative is to name the site out of scope in v4_06 with a candidate lane, under a lead ruling.

answers.composers_above_column_top: None by reading. Composers (FirstFit, Knuth-Plass, AdobeSingleLine, AdobeParagraph, and CJK through the same slots) only break into slots. Every slot baseline comes from next_slot, floored at :458, with the guard at :394-398, or from balance_band, floored at :900-911 with the same guard. The snap path can sit below base by at most EPS * step, which is negligible. The anchor push adds only pre > 0 (:1184). vertical_justify can move lines down past the bottom (F1) but never above the top: the first line by index sits at the column's first baseline or lower, and dy >= 0 whenever the block fits.
answers.overset_paths: Compose: correct. A lifted paragraph steps down from the column top, next_slot moves lines that do not fit to the next column or frame (extra and first reset), and overset starts at the first paragraph that gets no slot (probe: 30..119). Threaded frames: same mechanism, by reading; untested (F3c). Balancing: runs only when overset is None, re-adds gaps with the floor, and refuses (moves nothing) when a row would pass the bottom. Anchors: the floor comes before the push (:1180 then :1186), and a push past the bottom is re-applied at the next column's top with extra = pre. Vertical justification: wrong, because lines can leave the frame with overset None (F1).
answers.legit_negative_space_unchanged: Yes. floored bites only when extra < -(line * height), which is equivalent to base + line * height + extra < base, the formula baseline_of uses. It changes only layouts in which some line would sit above the column's first baseline. Later lines move only after such a bite: the dropped part of the gap is not carried. The kept test space_before_and_after_add_one_gap_dropped_at_a_column_top (10, 32, 42) is untouched by reading, because -6 never reaches the floor.
answers.nan_infinity: Handled. space_before and space_after pass through length_pt (styles.rs:75, finite only), so gap is finite or refused by sum (:1138 at a7de5fcd). Flow-record before and after pass through pt() (folio_input.rs:99-104, finite) and nonneg. floored never sees NaN. line * height can only overflow to +inf, which gives a floor of -inf, no clamp, and a baseline past the bottom, so the line moves to the next column. balance_band checks extra.is_finite() before the floor. The unchecked `c.extra += pre[pi]` can only reach +inf, which is a push past the frame. Removing Cursor.gaps reopens nothing, because the floor bounds extra from below and positive sums are still checked by sum.
answers.v4_06_sites: 13 of 14 are correct by reading. The count of 6 fixed and 8 not applicable is correct. The span and split before and after sites are not applicable (larger() with a flow value >= 0, paragraph_flows nonneg :804-807). The snap delta is >= -EPS * step. break_target and the column/frame resets use extra 0. The anchor site is fixed by ordering. vertical_justify is wrongly marked not applicable (F1): it is not paragraph space, but it relies on a monotone column, which negative paragraph space breaks.
answers.tests_vs_implementation: Mostly behaviour. The probe port asserts min baseline >= the first line's and overset Some, then pins the Studio reading (exact baselines, overset 30..119). The anchor test distinguishes the gap-site floor. The updated hostile case asserts behaviour (Ok, finite, nothing above the first line, 10/10/10, overset None). Its overset None, which deviates from the ruling's wording, is correct for that story by reading: three one-line paragraphs all land on 10. Weak spots: the balancing and smaller-leading tests are satisfied by the guard alone (F3), and no vertical-justification or threaded case exists (F1, F3c).
